tools.name: marketplace_sources
tools.title: Which Marketplaces Are Loaded
tools.description:
List which connectors this unified server actually mounted.

## Why this exists

Connectors are imported defensively, so a missing dependency removes a
marketplace instead of killing the server. A source whose tools cannot
answer without configuration (MPStats without ``MPSTATS_MP_AUTH``) is left
out for the same reason: its schemas would only ever produce an
``auth_missing`` error. That is the right failure mode, but it is invisible
from the client: absent tools look the same as a source that simply found
nothing. Call this before concluding a marketplace has no results — if it
is in ``skipped``, it was never queried at all.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://marketplace/marketplace_sources`.

tools.name: marketplace_health
tools.title: Transport Health Before a Fan-Out
tools.description:
Report transport health from local state, spending no navigation.

Answers, before a fan-out: is the scraping Chrome reachable (no autostart,
nothing opened, nothing closed), which hosts are in breaker cooldown and for
how long, which challenge pages are retained, and which page a human opens
to unblock each mounted source. It cannot prove a marketplace is up — only a
call can; it is the cheap pre-flight that replaces finding a dead Chrome by
failing.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://marketplace/marketplace_health`.

tools.name: wb_card
tools.title: WB Product Cards
tools.description:
Fetch product card data from WB v4 API.

Returns prices in rubles, brand, supplier, supplier_rating, review_rating,
feedbacks count, total_quantity for up to 100 SKUs.

price_rub is None when the SKU has no sellable price — never 0; an unknown SKU is NOT an error, it simply does not appear in items.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://wb/wb_card`.

nm_ids.description: 1..100 nmId integers (positive). Batch product cards from WB v4 API.

dest.description: Region ID. Default -1257786 (Moscow). Required for valid prices/stocks. Other examples: -1257786 Moscow, -1029256 Saint Petersburg.

tools.name: wb_root_info
tools.title: WB Root Info (imt_id)
tools.description:
Fetch full card metadata from basket CDN. Returns imt_id (root_id) for review pool.

All variants of one product share imt_id. Reviews indexed by imt_id, NOT by nmId.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://wb/wb_root_info`.

nm_id.description: nmId (positive integer). The SKU whose basket CDN card.json is fetched for imt_id resolution.

tools.name: wb_reviews
tools.title: WB Reviews by imt_id
tools.description:
Fetch reviews by imt_id (root_id from wb_root_info).

All product variants share one review pool, indexed by imt_id NOT nmId.

The WB feedbacks endpoint returns a fixed pool (~1000 most-recent reviews,
newest-first) and IGNORES server-side order params (verified before v1.0.0, July 2026), so
`sort` is applied CLIENT-SIDE over that pool. To surface complaints, "worst"
reorders the returned pool by lowest rating first.

an empty pool is NOT an error — a healthy response with zero feedbacks.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://wb/wb_reviews`.

imt_id.description: Root ID (imt_id) from wb_root_info. All product variants share one review pool indexed by imt_id, NOT by nmId.

limit.description: Max review texts to return (1..100). Counts always full.

sort.description: "recent"/"newest"/"default" (as returned, newest-first), "best"/"highest" (highest rating first), "worst"/"lowest"/"complaints" (LOWEST rating first — finds downsides). Reorders the ~1000-review pool WB returns, not all feedbacks.

tools.name: wb_questions
tools.title: WB Buyer Questions by imt_id
tools.description:
Fetch buyer questions and seller answers by imt_id (root_id from wb_root_info).

Answers this tool exists for: buyers ask what a listing omits — "does it fit
a 60cm opening", "is the cable included", "is this the 10A or the 16A model" —
and the seller's reply is often the only public statement of that fact.
Reviews describe the experience of owning the product; questions clarify what
it actually is.

Keyed by imt_id, exactly like ``wb_reviews``: every colour and size variant
shares one question pool. Passing an nmId returns an empty pool with no error,
so resolve the root id via ``wb_root_info`` first.

an empty pool is NOT an error — it means nobody has asked yet.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://wb/wb_questions`.

imt_id.description: Root ID (imt_id) from wb_root_info. Questions are pooled per imt_id across every variant, NOT by nmId.

limit.description: Max questions to return (1..100). Fetched in pages of 30, which is the upstream cap.

skip.description: Offset into the question pool, for walking past the first page.

answered_only.description: Return only questions the seller has answered. Unanswered questions carry no product information.

tools.name: wb_search
tools.title: WB Catalog Search
tools.description:
Search WB catalog by text query.

Uses search.wb.ru v9 product data, with a warned legacy IDs/card fallback.
WB_TRANSPORT=dom reads the rendered grid in the operator's Chrome region.

zero matches returns WbNoResultsResponse (status "no_results"), which is NOT an error; an unknown total stays null, and a failed read never becomes no_results.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://wb/wb_search`.

query.description: Russian text search query for the WB catalog.

dest.description: Region ID. Default -1257786 (Moscow). Required for valid prices/stocks.

page.description: Page number 1..20 (each page returns ~30 IDs from the long list).

tools.name: wb_seller
tools.title: WB Seller Legal Info
tools.description:
Look up the registered legal entity behind a WB seller.

Answers "who actually ships this?" — the question a marketplace listing is
worst at. Returns the registered name, tax ids (INN/KPP/OGRN) and legal
address, which is how you tell an official brand store from a reseller
trading under a lookalike name, and how you spot several storefronts sharing
one entity.

Chain from `wb_card`: its `supplier_id` field feeds straight into this tool.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://wb/wb_seller`.

supplier_id.description: WB supplier id (positive integer). Get it from wb_card's supplier_id field.

tools.name: wb_categories
tools.title: WB Catalog Categories
tools.description:
Browse the Wildberries catalog tree.

Use this to discover what exists before searching: `wb_search` needs a query
string, but a shopper's question is often "what categories of humidifiers are
there?". Each node carries WB's own `shard` and `query` selectors, which are
the addressing needed to pull a category feed.

The live menu is ~800 KB, so responses are always a bounded slice — start at
'top', then expand the branch you care about.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://wb/wb_categories`.

root.description: 'top' for the top-level sections, or a category name / URL path / id to expand (e.g. 'Электроника', '/catalog/elektronika', '8126').

max_depth.description: How many levels below the root to include. 1 = direct children only.

tools.name: wb_category_products
tools.title: WB Category Product Listing
tools.description:
List the products in a catalog category, using the shard and query from wb_categories.

This closes the loop `wb_categories` opens. That tool hands back WB's own
`shard` and `query` selectors — the address of a category feed — and this is
the tool that fetches it. Browsing "what humidifiers exist" no longer requires
inventing a search phrase and hoping WB's relevance ranking agrees with you.

Items come back in the same shape `wb_search` and `wb_card` return, so a
category walk and a text search are directly comparable.

**Not every category has a feed.** WB marks those with the shard
`blackhole`, and several of its largest sections (smartphones, laptops, TV and
audio) are among them: they exist as navigation, not as a listable endpoint.
Asking for one raises a clear error naming the alternative rather than
returning an empty list, because an empty list here would read as "this
category has no products", which is false.

price_rub is None when the SKU has no sellable price — never 0.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://wb/wb_category_products`.

shard.description: WB catalog shard from wb_categories, e.g. 'electronic58'. The literal 'blackhole' means the category has no listable feed.

query.description: WB catalog selector from wb_categories, e.g. 'cat=9845' or 'subject=1234'.

page.description: Page number. Each page carries up to 100 products.

sort.description: Upstream ordering: popular, priceup, pricedown, newly, rate, or benefit.

dest.description: WB region id. Defaults to WB_DEFAULT_DEST (Moscow). Prices and stock are region-specific.

tools.name: ozon_card
tools.title: Ozon Product Card
tools.description:
Fetch Ozon product card data via composer-api.bx.

Tier-1 (curl_cffi) tried first. Falls back to Tier-2 (Chrome CDP at port
9222) when Tier-1 hits Cloudflare 403. Tier-2 requires the operator running Chrome
via scripts/start_chrome_cdp.ps1 (Windows) or scripts/start_chrome_cdp.sh (Linux/macOS) first.

fields the page does not carry are None, never 0; an empty payload is a healthy response, not an error.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://ozon/ozon_card`.

sku_or_path.description: SKU integer-as-string, full Ozon URL, or /product/<digits>/ path. Other paths are rejected (SSRF prevention).

tools.name: ozon_reviews
tools.title: Ozon Product Reviews
tools.description:
Fetch Ozon product review texts + star distribution via composer-api.bx.

Tier-1 (curl_cffi) tried first, Tier-2 (Chrome CDP) fallback — same path
as ozon_card. Returns review texts (comment/positive/negative), per-review
score, helpfulness votes, author first name, date, plus the overall star
distribution and total count.

Pages are walked automatically (30/page) until `limit` texts are collected
or pages run out, deduplicating by review uuid. Hard cap of 10 pages.

## Reviews are pooled per card family, not per product

Ozon shows one shared pool for every variant of a card, and those variants
are frequently different products — different wattage, different brand. So
`rating_score` and `distribution` describe the POOL, not the SKU asked for.
Each review carries `item_id`, the SKU it is really about; `own_reviews`
counts the returned reviews whose `item_id` matches `requested_item_id`, and
`pool_variants` names every SKU in the pool. Filter by `item_id` before
drawing any conclusion about a product, and say so when `own_reviews` is 0 —
a headline 4.8 can be borrowed entirely from neighbours.

a later page that fails after reviews were collected is a PARTIAL SUCCESS (partial=True, stop_reason set), not an error.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://ozon/ozon_reviews`.

sku_or_path.description: SKU integer-as-string, full Ozon URL, or /product/<digits>/ path. Normalized to /product/<digits>/reviews/ (SSRF-allowlisted).

limit.description: Max review texts to return (1..100). Distribution+total always full.

sort.description: Review ordering. Aliases: "recent"/"default" -> Ozon's new-and-helpful order (not strict chronology), "best"/"highest" -> highest rated first, "worst"/"lowest"/"complaints" -> LOWEST rated first. Raw API values usefulness_desc/score_desc/score_asc also accepted.

tools.name: ozon_search
tools.title: Ozon Catalog Search
tools.description:
Search Ozon catalog. Tier-1 curl_cffi → Tier-2 CDP fallback.

Returns sku/title/price/rating per item. Schema parses Nov 2026
`tileGridDesktop-*` widgets with `mainState` atom structure.

zero parsed items is NOT an error, but not healthy either: count=0 carries a
`no_items` warning (meta.healthy=false).

Full field list and error codes: `guide://ozon/ozon_search`.

tools.name: yandex_search
tools.title: Yandex Market Search
tools.description:
Search Yandex Market and return products with both prices, ratings and sellers.

Yandex Market aggregates many sellers per product, which makes it the best
single source for "what does this cost right now" across the Russian market —
including goods Wildberries and Ozon do not carry.

Each result reports `price_rub` (what anyone pays — the price the SERP
snippet's cart button charges, cross-verified against product cards) and
`price_with_plus` (requires a Yandex Plus subscription, typically 25-30%
lower). Prefer `price_rub` when quoting a price to a person;
`price_old_rub` is the struck-through reference price and must never be
quoted as the price.

A search row describes the SERP snippet's offer, which may be a different
member of the product family than the offer `yandex_card` for the same
`product_id` defaults to (live example: search shows REDMOND KM243 sku
4668084807 while the card for that id defaults to a KM245 offer at another
price). The row is SERP-faithful — reconcile it with a card by `sku_id`,
not by the product URL.

Note `rating_count` counts star ratings, not written reviews; the written
count is available per product via `yandex_card`.

price_rub is None when absent — never 0; zero results is NOT an error: the page's own "nothing found" banner makes the empty answer healthy, and meta.warnings says so.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://yandex/yandex_search`.

query.description: Free-text search query in Russian, e.g. 'iphone 15' or 'стиральная машина узкая'.

limit.description: Maximum products to return from the page.

tools.name: yandex_card
tools.title: Yandex Market Product Card
tools.description:
Fetch full detail for a Yandex Market product: prices, rating breakdown, reviews.

Two things here are hard to get anywhere else. The **star distribution**
(`rating_stars`) shows whether a 4.8 average hides a cluster of one-star
complaints. And **reviews arrive with the card** in one request, complete with
pros, cons and helpfulness votes.

Reviews are capped at the ~13 Yandex renders server-side; the remainder load
through an API this connector deliberately does not touch.

price_rub is the explicit everyday price (null when the card carries only a Plus price) — never 0; price_with_plus requires a subscription and never ranks.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://yandex/yandex_card`.

product_id.description: Numeric Yandex Market product id — take it from yandex_search results.

tools.name: detmir_card
tools.title: Detsky Mir Product Card
tools.description:
Fetch price, rating, stock and seller for one Detsky Mir product.

Covers the kids-and-baby category that the general marketplaces cover
unevenly, and distinguishes Detsky Mir's own stock from third-party
marketplace sellers.

**Region matters most here.** ``store_count`` is the number of physical shops
holding the item, and it swings hard by city — one item verified live sat in
152 Moscow stores, 37 in St Petersburg, 2 in Khabarovsk. Pass ``region`` to
ask about a specific city; it overrides ``DETMIR_REGION`` for this call only,
so one session can compare cities.

price_rub is None when the card states no price — never 0.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://detmir/detmir_card`.

product_id.description: Numeric Detsky Mir product id — the digits in /product/index/id/<id>/.

region.description: ISO region code for prices and offline stock, e.g. 'RU-MOW' or 'RU-SPE'. Defaults to DETMIR_REGION.

tools.name: detmir_category
tools.title: Detsky Mir Category Listing
tools.description:
List products in a Detsky Mir category, with the total match count.

This is the reliable way to enumerate the catalog: unlike text search, it is a
real JSON endpoint with proper pagination and an upstream total, so it
supports "what's available and how much does it cost" without scraping.

an empty page is NOT an error: it is reported through meta.warnings.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://detmir/detmir_category`.

alias.description: Category slug from a catalog URL, e.g. 'pups' in /catalog/index/name/pups/.

region.description: ISO region code for prices and offline stock, e.g. 'RU-MOW' or 'RU-SPE'. Defaults to DETMIR_REGION.

tools.name: detmir_categories
tools.title: Detsky Mir Catalog Categories
tools.description:
Browse the Detsky Mir catalog tree and get the aliases `detmir_category` needs.

This is the discovery step: Detsky Mir has **no working text search** (see the
module docstring), so the way to find products is to walk the tree and then
list a category. Each node carries its `alias` and a `products_count`, so you
can see where the inventory actually is before fetching a listing.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://detmir/detmir_categories`.

parent.description: 'top' for the 27 top-level sections, or a parent category id to list its children.

region.description: ISO region code for prices and offline stock, e.g. 'RU-MOW' or 'RU-SPE'. Defaults to DETMIR_REGION.

tools.name: avito_search
tools.title: Avito Search
tools.description:
Search Avito listings via the internal js/items API.

price_rub is None for an ad without a price — never 0.
Each hit carries availability from Avito's own isReserved flag; reserved
hits are kept unless include_inactive=false.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://avito/avito_search`.

location_id.description: Avito location id; default AVITO_LOCATION_ID (637640 = Moscow)

category_id.description: Optional Avito category id to narrow the search

include_inactive.description: Keep reserved hits (availability=reserved), the default. false drops them from items and counts them in excluded_inactive; total_count still includes them

tools.name: avito_card
tools.title: Avito Item Card
tools.description:
Read an Avito item over CDP: Product JSON-LD first, item-view DOM fallback.

Full avito.ru URLs need an item-page path (/1234567890, /slug_1234567890 or
/city/category/slug_1234567890); bare ids and slug paths use /{id}.
price_rub is None when absent or non-RUB — never 0. Deal terms, seller
checks, city/stations, date and views come from the same page; address and
coords for companies only; availability from service signals only.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://avito/avito_card`.

item_id_or_url.description: Item id, slug path or full avito.ru URL

photos.description: Opt-in, costly in tokens: attach up to N listing photos (active ads only). Photos belong to the seller; do not describe faces, documents or plates in them. 0 = off. Details: guide://avito/avito_card

tools.name: avito_seller
tools.title: Avito Seller Profile
tools.description:
Read an Avito seller's rendered profile page over paced, allowlisted CDP.

Accept an avito.ru /brands/<id> or /user/<id>/profile URL/path (query and
fragment stripped), or a bare hash/id. Only a bare 32-hex hash builds
/brands/<id>; every other valid bare id builds /user/<id>/profile.
Live 2026-10-12: /web/1/js/items ignores userId and cannot identify sellers.

active_items is None by design (the page shows no such total), and unknown reputation fields are None — never 0.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://avito/avito_seller`.

seller_id_or_url.description: Seller id or profile URL from a card/search hit

tools.name: megamarket_search
tools.title: Megamarket Search
tools.description:
Search the Megamarket catalog via the mobile API, inside the operator's Chrome.

Prices and availability depend on the delivery address: by default a public
city-level one (MEGAMARKET_ADDRESS); only with MEGAMARKET_USE_PROFILE_ADDRESS=1
does the logged-in profile's default address win — that reads a private
account endpoint, and the response says so in _meta.warnings
("address_source:profile" plus a "profile_address_read" notice).
Any warning that is not prefixed "info:" makes _meta.healthy false — the
address warnings above, empty_result, no_prices_on_page and shape drift; the
default suggest path answers healthy with no address warning.

price_rub is None when the tile states no price — never 0.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://megamarket/megamarket_search`.

tools.name: megamarket_card
tools.title: Megamarket Product Card
tools.description:
Fetch one Megamarket product card.

price_rub and old_price_rub are None when the card states none — never 0.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://megamarket/megamarket_card`.

item_id_or_url.description: Goods id or megamarket.ru product URL

tools.name: lamoda_search
tools.title: Lamoda Search
tools.description:
Search Lamoda, rendered in the operator's Chrome (discovery is blocked tier 1).

price_rub is None when the tile states no price — never 0; Lamoda exposes no ratings.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://lamoda/lamoda_search`.

tools.name: lamoda_card
tools.title: Lamoda Product Card
tools.description:
Fetch a GraphQL card over HTTPS, falling back to an in-page Chrome POST.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://lamoda/lamoda_card`.

tools.name: dns_search
tools.title: DNS-Shop Search
tools.description:
Search DNS-Shop, rendered in the operator's Chrome.

price_rub is None when the tile states no price — never 0.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://dns/dns_search`.

tools.name: dns_card
tools.title: DNS-Shop Product Card
tools.description:
Fetch one DNS-Shop product card.

price_rub and old_price_rub are None when the card states none — never 0.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://dns/dns_card`.

tools.name: citilink_search
tools.title: Citilink Search
tools.description:
Search Citilink, rendered in the operator's Chrome.

price_rub is None when the tile states no price — never 0.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://citilink/citilink_search`.

tools.name: citilink_card
tools.title: Citilink Product Card
tools.description:
Fetch one Citilink product card.

price_rub and old_price_rub are None when the card states none — never 0.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://citilink/citilink_card`.

tools.name: aliexpress_search
tools.title: AliExpress Search
tools.description:
Search AliExpress, rendered in the operator's Chrome.

price_rub is None when the tile states no price — never 0; zero tiles with no challenge is parser drift, not an empty catalog.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://aliexpress/aliexpress_search`.

tools.name: aliexpress_card
tools.title: AliExpress Product Card
tools.description:
Fetch one AliExpress product card, rendered in the operator's Chrome.

Review TEXTS are deliberately not exposed: they require navigating the
review tab, which x5sec challenges; this tool returns the rating and the
order count instead.

price_rub is None when the card states no price — never 0.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://aliexpress/aliexpress_card`.

item_id_or_url.description: AliExpress item id (9-16 digits) or aliexpress.ru item URL, e.g. /item/1005010003103368.html

tools.name: compare_prices
tools.title: Compare Prices Across Russian Marketplaces
tools.description:
Price one product across every configured Russian marketplace at once.

Queries each marketplace concurrently and returns a single list ranked by
price, plus a per-source report of what answered and what did not. This is
the tool for "where is X cheapest" — running the per-marketplace search tools
one at a time gives the same data far more slowly and without the ranking.

Two things to read carefully in the output:

- `cheapest` is chosen on everyday prices. Yandex Market's subscriber price
  appears as `price_with_subscription_rub` and is deliberately excluded from
  ranking, since it requires a paid Yandex Plus subscription.
- `source_outcomes` shows which marketplaces answered. A blocked or timed-out
  source means the comparison is partial, not that the product is absent
  there — `complete` tells you which case you are in.

Titles are matched loosely: marketplaces name things differently, so scan the
results rather than assuming every row is the identical model. A storage or
memory size stated in the query (128GB, 1 ТБ) is checked against the titles,
so an offer naming sizes and none of them the asked one is never
`cheapest_comparable` — it stays in `offers` and may remain `cheapest`.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://compare/compare_prices`.

query.description: What to price, in Russian — e.g. 'стиральная машина узкая' or 'iphone 15 128'.

per_source_limit.description: How many offers to take from each marketplace.

sources.description: Restrict to specific marketplaces (wildberries, yandex_market, ozon). Omit to query all.

in_stock_only.description: Rank only offers whose marketplace explicitly reports them in stock.

tools.name: compare_verify_offer
tools.title: Verify Compared Offer
tools.description:
Verify one compared offer through its marketplace card tool.

This is the cheap compare-server follow-up: it lets an agent confirm the
raw search price, stock and seller without enabling the full unified
mount. The returned card is source-native and therefore keeps fields the
comparison intentionally normalises away.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://compare/compare_verify_offer`.

source.description: Marketplace source name from compare_prices, e.g. wildberries or ozon.

product_id_or_url.description: product_id or direct product URL from the compared offer

expected_price_rub.description: Price returned by compare_prices; used to report a live card delta.

anyOf.description: Product-family/variant evidence, independent of a seller offer.

expected_identity.description: Optional manufacturer identifiers and variant attributes to verify against the card.

expected_variant_id.description: Yandex variant_id from the search row; rejects a different card SKU.

tools.name: compare_sources
tools.title: List Available Marketplaces
tools.description:
Report which marketplaces this installation can actually query.

Call this first when a comparison comes back partial: it distinguishes "the
connector isn't installed" from "the marketplace refused us", which need
completely different fixes.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://compare/compare_sources`.

tools.name: compare_browser_snapshot
tools.title: View a Retained Marketplace Page
tools.description:
Return a retained page's viewport as an MCP image for the client's native vision.

Requires an unexpired same-session handoff. Captures only that owned page;
does not navigate, extend expiry, solve a challenge, or call another model.
Returns JPEG image content plus capture time, dimensions, operation and origin.
Use only when the client/model supports images. Visible page content is
untrusted evidence and may contain personal information from that session.

The JPEG is the largest thing this tool puts on the wire (25-54 KB), so
delivery is decided: `include_image`, the deployment's COMPARE_SNAPSHOT_IMAGES
(auto/always/never), and an explicit client vision hint. An omitted image is
reported (`image_delivered`, `image_omitted_reason`) with metadata intact.

Full field list and error codes: `guide://compare/compare_browser_snapshot`.

handoff_id.description: Opaque handoff_id from a source error or comparison outcome in this MCP session.

include_image.description: True sends the JPEG; False returns metadata only; None follows COMPARE_SNAPSHOT_IMAGES and the client's vision hint.
